question: One of the following statements about the epidemiology and prognosis of heart failure is INCORRECT. Point it out

options.opa: Between 60 and 70% of patients die in the first 5 years after establishing the diagnosis of heart failure.
options.opb: The functional situation of the patient with heart failure is the one that best correlates with the expectation of survival.
options.opc: Diastolic dysfunction predominates in elderly women with a history of chronic hypertension.
options.opd: Heart failure due to systolic dysfunction is usually observed in male patients with ischemic heart disease.
options.ope: The prevalence of heart failure is decreasing in the last decade thanks to better control of cardiovascular risk factors.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Patients with heart failure may have a reduced ejection fraction -> Reduced ejection fraction is associated with systolic dysfunction -> Systolic dysfunction is more common in male patients with ischemic heart disease -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Diastolic dysfunction is characterized by impaired relaxation or increased stiffness of the heart -> Diastolic dysfunction is more common in elderly women with a history of chronic hypertension -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: The prognosis of heart failure can be influenced by the functional status of the patient -> Functional status correlates with the expectation of survival -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Improved control of cardiovascular risk factors can lead to a decrease in the prevalence of heart failure -> Better control of risk factors may impact the epidemiology of heart failure -> 75% confidence. CHAIN: The statement that between 60 and -> 80%
enhanced_information: The statement in option opa is incorrect. The correct epidemiology and prognosis of heart failure indicate that not between 60 and 70% of patients die in the first 5 years after establishing the diagnosis of heart failure. This statement contradicts the typical survival rates seen in heart failure patients.
analysis: The core medical principle in heart failure epidemiology and prognosis is that the statement in option opa is incorrect. The survival rates in heart failure patients do not typically show such high mortality rates within the first 5 years. The most likely correct option is opa.
